_note: Concept graph connecting frontier ideas to channel pillars, audience states, human situations, forms of help, production grammar and risks. Affinity values are editorial priors, not scientific measurements.

constructed_emotion.desired_movement: From treating a feeling as a verdict to examining it as a body-informed prediction.
practical_tests: Name the sensation, the prediction and the evidence separately.
constructed_emotion.evidence_boundary: Constructed-emotion theory is influential and evidence-based but debated; it does not mean feelings are imaginary or freely chosen.
risk_mitigations: Validate the feeling as real experience.
Never imply a person chose symptoms.
constructed_emotion.grounding: Feel the chair, notice one body signal, and name only what is observable.

confabulation.desired_movement: From confident self-explanation to honest curiosity about causes.
practical_tests: Write the reason you gave, then list what happened before the reason appeared.
confabulation.evidence_boundary: People can report genuine reasons; interpreter and choice-blindness findings show that confidence does not guarantee access to the full cause.
risk_mitigations: Do not claim all reasons are fake.
Use uncertainty to increase responsibility, not erase it.
confabulation.grounding: Return to one decision made today and separate sequence from explanation.

avoid: literal brain spokesperson for every scene

placebo_belief.desired_movement: From belief as harmless opinion or magical cure to belief as one measurable influence among many.
practical_tests: Notice the expectation attached to a symptom without changing prescribed care.
placebo_belief.evidence_boundary: Placebo and nocebo effects are real but bounded; they do not show that belief cures every illness or that sickness is a failure of mindset.
risk_mitigations: State explicitly that belief is not a substitute for treatment.
placebo_belief.grounding: Separate the symptom, the expectation, and the medical evidence on the table.

other_minds.desired_movement: From arguing with a simulated person to checking the available evidence and asking.
practical_tests: List what they did, what you inferred, and what would change the inference.
other_minds.evidence_boundary: Social cognition relies on models, but another person is not reducible to your model and retains their own account.
risk_mitigations: A model can be incomplete while harm remains real.
Do not use uncertainty to override boundaries or testimony.
other_minds.grounding: Return to the exact words, action, time and place before the interpretation.

memory_is_future.desired_movement: From the past as a fixed sentence to noticing which pieces are being used to simulate tomorrow.
practical_tests: Name one remembered image currently furnishing a feared future.
memory_is_future.evidence_boundary: Remembering and imagining share systems, but this does not mean memory alone determines the future or that painful memories are voluntary.
risk_mitigations: Do not promise re-authoring will erase trauma.
memory_is_future.grounding: Notice the present room and one object that was not in the memory.

jamais_vu.desired_movement: From familiarity as invisibility to direct astonishment at an ordinary thing.
practical_tests: Repeat a harmless familiar word slowly and notice when the familiarity changes.
jamais_vu.evidence_boundary: Semantic satiation and jamais vu are documented experiences; the exercise reveals altered familiarity, not hidden metaphysical reality.
risk_mitigations: Keep the experiment brief and ordinary.
jamais_vu.grounding: Name five ordinary details in the room after the experiment.

avoid: claims that the world is fake

binding_continuity.desired_movement: From accepting a seamless story to inspecting the separate inputs and missing cuts.
practical_tests: Separate observations, sources, cuts and inferred continuity.
binding_continuity.evidence_boundary: Perceptual binding and change blindness show construction; they do not prove an inner editor is a literal entity.
risk_mitigations: Use source-checking rather than blanket distrust.
binding_continuity.grounding: Look at the actual cup, sound and room before the story connecting them.

aphantasia_varieties.desired_movement: From assuming one standard inner experience to asking how another mind actually renders.
practical_tests: Ask someone to describe whether an imagined apple is seen, known, heard or absent.
aphantasia_varieties.evidence_boundary: Self-reported imagery and inner speech vary widely; categories are useful but not complete maps of a person.
risk_mitigations: Let people describe their own experience.
aphantasia_varieties.grounding: Ask a real person and listen without correcting their description.

agency_time.desired_movement: From total helplessness to one proportionate act that changes the felt relation between cause and effect.
practical_tests: Choose one action that produces a visible effect within ten minutes and notice the felt interval.
agency_time.evidence_boundary: Temporal binding is a laboratory effect; it does not mean action literally changes clock time or that every delay is solved by effort.
risk_mitigations: Use small agency, not total control.
Call clock-warping a metaphor outside the experiment.
agency_time.grounding: Press one real button, move one real object, observe one real result.

moving_subjects: clock gears bending around a hand

entropic_brain.desired_movement: From metaphysical certainty about a trip to grounded curiosity about loosened predictions and lived meaning.
practical_tests: Recall what changed in perception, then separate experience, interpretation and evidence.
entropic_brain.evidence_boundary: Relaxed-priors and entropic-brain accounts are active scientific models; they do not establish that psychedelic content reveals an external metaphysical realm.
risk_mitigations: Use care language for destabilizing experiences.
entropic_brain.grounding: Return to the chair, breath, wet cheeks, clock and ordinary room.

body_ownership.desired_movement: From a rigid or frightening self-border to curiosity about how ownership is inferred and stabilized.
practical_tests: Notice pressure, temperature and position in the real hand without inducing an illusion.
body_ownership.evidence_boundary: Body ownership is experimentally malleable, but the rubber-hand illusion does not prove the self is unreal or boundaries do not matter.
risk_mitigations: Do not instruct vulnerable viewers to destabilize body ownership.
body_ownership.grounding: Feel the weight and temperature of the actual hand against the chair.

moving_subjects: brush strokes on rubber and real hand

narrative_self.desired_movement: From defending a fixed center to treating the self as a useful, revisable organization.
practical_tests: List three roles that changed while ordinary awareness and responsibility continued.
narrative_self.evidence_boundary: The narrative-self account is a philosophical and scientific framework; it does not settle whether consciousness has no deeper nature.
risk_mitigations: Useful fiction does not mean worthless or fake.
narrative_self.grounding: Notice the body reading, the room holding it, and the next ordinary responsibility.
